4//! Gaussian blur filter implementation using multi-scale separable convolution.
5//!
6//! This implementation uses a multi-scale approach for efficient blurring:
7//! - **Small blurs** (σ ≤ 2): Direct separable convolution at full resolution
8//! - **Large blurs** (σ > 2): Iterative downsample → blur → upsample pyramid
9//!
10//! The algorithm automatically determines the optimal number of decimation levels
11//! using variance analysis. Each 2× decimation applies a \[1,3,3,1\]/8 binomial filter
12//! (adding variance = 3.0), then downsamples, reducing the remaining blur work needed.
13//! This exploits the variance additivity property: `σ²_total = σ²_downsample + σ²_blur`.
14//!
15//! **Variance Addition Reference**: The convolution of two Gaussians with variances σ₁²
16//! and σ₂² produces a Gaussian with variance σ₁² + σ₂². This fundamental property comes
17//! from probability theory and applies to Gaussian convolution in image processing. See:
18//! - Torralba & Freeman, "Foundations of Computer Vision" (MIT Press), Section 2.2:
19//!   <https://visionbook.mit.edu/blurring_2.html#properties-of-the-continuous-gaussian>
20

30impl FilterEffect for GaussianBlur {
31    fn execute_lowp(&self, pixmap: &mut Pixmap, layer_manager: &mut LayerManager) {
32        // No blur if std_deviation is zero or negative
33        if self.std_deviation <= 0.0 {
34            return;
35        }
36
37        let scratch = layer_manager.get_scratch_buffer(pixmap.width(), pixmap.height());
38        apply_blur(pixmap, scratch, self.n_decimations, &self.kernel[..usize::from(self.kernel_size)], self.edge_mode);
39    }
40
41    fn execute_highp(&self, pixmap: &mut Pixmap, layer_manager: &mut LayerManager) {
42        // TODO: Currently only lowp is implemented and used for highp as well.
43        // This needs to be updated to use proper high-precision arithmetic.
44        Self::execute_lowp(self, pixmap, layer_manager);
45    }
46}

48/// Apply Gaussian blur using multi-scale decimation and upsampling.
49///
50/// Uses a precomputed decimation plan and kernel for optimal performance.
51/// Operates in-place using a single pixmap buffer with logical dimension tracking
52/// to minimize memory allocations. For `n_decimations=0`, applies direct convolution.
53///
54/// The `scratch` buffer is used for separable convolution and must be at least as
55/// large as the source pixmap.
56pub(crate) fn apply_blur(pixmap: &mut Pixmap, scratch: &mut Pixmap, n_decimations: usize, kernel: &[f32], edge_mode: EdgeMode) {
57    let radius = (kernel.len() / 2) as u8;
58    let width = pixmap.width();
59    let height = pixmap.height();
60
61    // Small blur: apply direct convolution at full resolution
62    if n_decimations == 0 {
63        convolve(pixmap, scratch, width, height, kernel, radius, edge_mode);
64        return;
65    }
66
67    // Track logical dimensions through decimation (physical buffer stays the same size)
68    let mut sizer = DecimationSizer::new(width, height);
69
70    // Downsample n times (each step reduces resolution by 2×)
71    for _ in 0..n_decimations {
72        let (w, h) = sizer.current();
73        downscale(pixmap, w, h, edge_mode);
74        sizer.downscale();
75    }
76
77    // Apply the reduced blur at the coarsest resolution
78    let (w, h) = sizer.current();
79    convolve(pixmap, scratch, w, h, kernel, radius, edge_mode);
80
81    // Upsample back to original resolution (each step doubles resolution by 2×)
82    for _ in 0..n_decimations {
83        let (w, h) = sizer.current();
84        upscale(pixmap, w, h, edge_mode);
85        sizer.upscale();
86    }
87
88    debug_assert_eq!(sizer.current(), (width, height), "Final dimensions should match original");
89}

91/// Apply separable Gaussian convolution with logical dimensions.
92///
93/// Performs horizontal blur followed by vertical blur. Works with a logical view
94/// of the pixmap, using only the top-left region defined by width × height.
95/// The `temp` buffer is provided by the caller to avoid allocations.
96pub(crate) fn convolve(src: &mut Pixmap, scratch: &mut Pixmap, width: u16, height: u16, kernel: &[f32], radius: u8, edge_mode: EdgeMode) {
97    convolve_x(src, scratch, width, height, kernel, radius, edge_mode);
98    convolve_y(scratch, src, width, height, kernel, radius, edge_mode);
99}
100
101/// Apply horizontal blur pass (1D convolution along x-axis).
102///
103/// For each output pixel, computes a weighted sum of horizontally neighboring pixels
104/// using the Gaussian kernel. Handles edge cases according to the specified edge mode.
105/// Writes results to a destination buffer to avoid overwriting source data.
106pub(crate) fn convolve_x(src: &Pixmap, dst: &mut Pixmap, src_width: u16, src_height: u16, kernel: &[f32], radius: u8, edge_mode: EdgeMode) {
107    for y in 0..src_height {
108        for x in 0..src_width {
109            let mut rgba = [0.0_f32; 4];
110
111            // Sum contributions from all kernel positions: output = Σ(weight[j] × pixel[x+j-radius])
112            for (j, &k) in kernel.iter().enumerate() {
113                #[expect(
114                    clippy::cast_possible_wrap,
115                    reason = "This cast never wraps because `kernel.len()` is never greater than `u8::MAX` due to the restriction on `MAX_KERNEL_SIZE`"
116                )]
117                let j = j as i32;
118                let src_x = x as i32 + j - radius as i32;
119                let p = sample_x(src, src_x, y, src_width, edge_mode);
120
121                rgba[0] += p.r as f32 * k;
122                rgba[1] += p.g as f32 * k;
123                rgba[2] += p.b as f32 * k;
124                rgba[3] += p.a as f32 * k;
125            }
126
127            // Convert back to u8 with rounding
128            dst.set_pixel(
129                x,
130                y,
131                PremulRgba8 { r: rgba[0].round() as u8, g: rgba[1].round() as u8, b: rgba[2].round() as u8, a: rgba[3].round() as u8 },
132            );
133        }
134    }
135}
136
137/// Apply vertical blur pass (1D convolution along y-axis).
138///
139/// For each output pixel, computes a weighted sum of vertically neighboring pixels
140/// using the Gaussian kernel. Handles edge cases according to the specified edge mode.
141/// Writes results to a destination buffer to avoid overwriting source data.
142pub(crate) fn convolve_y(src: &Pixmap, dst: &mut Pixmap, src_width: u16, src_height: u16, kernel: &[f32], radius: u8, edge_mode: EdgeMode) {
143    for y in 0..src_height {
144        for x in 0..src_width {
145            let mut rgba = [0.0_f32; 4];
146
147            // Sum contributions from all kernel positions: output = Σ(weight[j] × pixel[y+j-radius])
148            for (j, &k) in kernel.iter().enumerate() {
149                #[expect(
150                    clippy::cast_possible_wrap,
151                    reason = "This cast never wraps because `kernel.len()` is never greater than `u8::MAX` due to the restriction on `MAX_KERNEL_SIZE`"
152                )]
153                let j = j as i32;
154                let src_y = y as i32 + j - radius as i32;
155                let p = sample_y(src, x, src_y, src_height, edge_mode);
156
157                rgba[0] += p.r as f32 * k;
158                rgba[1] += p.g as f32 * k;
159                rgba[2] += p.b as f32 * k;
160                rgba[3] += p.a as f32 * k;
161            }
162
163            // Convert back to u8 with rounding
164            dst.set_pixel(
165                x,
166                y,
167                PremulRgba8 { r: rgba[0].round() as u8, g: rgba[1].round() as u8, b: rgba[2].round() as u8, a: rgba[3].round() as u8 },
168            );
169        }
170    }
171}

173/// Downsample image by 2x using separable \[1,3,3,1\]/8 binomial filter.
174///
175/// Performs horizontal and vertical decimation in sequence. Returns the new
176/// logical dimensions (ceil(width/2), ceil(height/2)).
177pub(crate) fn downscale(src: &mut Pixmap, src_width: u16, src_height: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) -> (u16, u16) {
178    let dst_width = src_width.div_ceil(2);
179    let dst_height = src_height.div_ceil(2);
180    downscale_x(src, src_width, src_height, dst_width, edge_mode);
181    // We can pass `dst_width` instead of `src_width` here, since we already decimated
182    // horizontally.
183    downscale_y(src, dst_width, src_height, dst_height, edge_mode);
184    (dst_width, dst_height)
185}
186
187/// Horizontal decimation pass using \[1,3,3,1\]/8 filter.
188///
189/// Reduces width by 2x while applying a binomial blur kernel. The \[1,3,3,1\] weights
190/// approximate a Gaussian and contribute variance=0.75 before the 2x downsampling.
191fn downscale_x(src: &mut Pixmap, src_width: u16, src_height: u16, dst_width: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) {
192    for y in 0..src_height {
193        // Sliding window: maintains 2 previous pixels (x0, x1) to form 4-tap filter
194        // with current pixels (x2, x3). Start with sample at -1 for implicit left padding.
195        let mut p0 = sample_x(src, -1, y, src_width, edge_mode);
196        let mut p1 = sample_x(src, 0, y, src_width, edge_mode);
197
198        for x in 0..dst_width {
199            // Sample 4 horizontally adjacent pixels for [1,3,3,1] kernel
200            // Pattern: [x*2-1, x*2, x*2+1, x*2+2]
201            let src_x = (x * 2) as i32;
202            let p2 = sample_x(src, src_x + 1, y, src_width, edge_mode);
203            let p3 = sample_x(src, src_x + 2, y, src_width, edge_mode);
204
205            // Apply [1,3,3,1]/8 weights → output = (p0 + 3×p1 + 3×p2 + p3) / 8
206            src.set_pixel(x, y, decimate_weighted(p0, p1, p2, p3));
207
208            // Advance window: previous p2,p3 become next p0,p1
209            p0 = p2;
210            p1 = p3;
211        }
212    }
213}
214
215/// Vertical decimation pass using \[1,3,3,1\]/8 filter.
216///
217/// Reduces logical height by 2x while applying a binomial blur kernel.
218/// Operates in-place by writing to the beginning of the same buffer.
219fn downscale_y(src: &mut Pixmap, src_width: u16, src_height: u16, dst_height: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) {
220    for x in 0..src_width {
221        // Sliding window: maintains 2 previous pixels (y0, y1) to form 4-tap filter
222        // with current pixels (y2, y3). Start with sample at -1 for implicit top padding.
223        let mut p0 = sample_y(src, x, -1, src_height, edge_mode);
224        let mut p1 = sample_y(src, x, 0, src_height, edge_mode);
225
226        for y in 0..dst_height {
227            // Sample 4 vertically adjacent pixels for [1,3,3,1] kernel
228            // Pattern: [y*2-1, y*2, y*2+1, y*2+2]
229            let src_y = (y * 2) as i32;
230            let p2 = sample_y(src, x, src_y + 1, src_height, edge_mode);
231            let p3 = sample_y(src, x, src_y + 2, src_height, edge_mode);
232
233            // Apply [1,3,3,1]/8 weights → output = (p0 + 3×p1 + 3×p2 + p3) / 8
234            src.set_pixel(x, y, decimate_weighted(p0, p1, p2, p3));
235
236            // Advance window: previous p2,p3 become next p0,p1
237            p0 = p2;
238            p1 = p3;
239        }
240    }
241}

243/// Upsample a pixmap by 2x using linear interpolation with [0.75, 0.25] weights.
244///
245/// Uses separable passes: horizontal doubling followed by vertical doubling.
246///
247/// ## Phase Alignment Theory
248///
249/// The downsampling \[1,3,3,1\]/8 filter creates a half-pixel offset. Its center of mass
250/// is at position `2k + 0.5`, not `2k`. This means each downsampled pixel at discrete
251/// position `k` represents a sample at continuous position `2k + 0.5`.
252///
253/// When upsampling, we reconstruct pixels at positions `2k` and `2k+1` from downsampled
254/// pixels whose centers are at `..., 2k-1.5, 2k+0.5, 2k+2.5, ...`
255///
256/// **Interpolation weights** are derived from linear interpolation based on distances:
257/// - Position `2k`:   distance 0.5 from center at `2k+0.5`, distance 1.5 from center at `2k-1.5`
258///   → weights: 0.75×pixel\[k\] + 0.25×pixel\[k-1\]
259/// - Position `2k+1`: distance 0.5 from center at `2k+0.5`, distance 1.5 from center at `2k+2.5`
260///   → weights: 0.75×pixel\[k\] + 0.25×pixel\[k+1\]
261pub(crate) fn upscale(src: &mut Pixmap, src_width: u16, src_height: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) -> (u16, u16) {
262    let dst_width = src_width * 2;
263    let dst_height = src_height * 2;
264    upscale_x(src, src_width, src_height, edge_mode);
265    upscale_y(src, dst_width, src_height, edge_mode);
266    (dst_width, dst_height)
267}
268
269/// Horizontal upsampling pass using [0.75, 0.25] interpolation with logical dimensions.
270///
271/// Doubles the logical width using phase-aligned interpolation. Each input pixel
272/// generates two output pixels with different weights based on their distance from
273/// the downsampled pixel's center position.
274/// Operates in-place by processing backwards to avoid overwriting source data.
275fn upscale_x(src: &mut Pixmap, src_width: u16, src_height: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) {
276    // Process backwards (right to left) to avoid overwriting source data
277    for y in 0..src_height {
278        // Maintain sliding window of three pixels: prev, current, next
279        // This allows us to compute both output pixels that depend on current pixel x
280        let mut p0 = sample_x(src, src_width as i32, y, src_width, edge_mode);
281        let mut p1 = sample_x(src, src_width as i32 - 1, y, src_width, edge_mode);
282
283        for x in (0..src_width).rev() {
284            let src_x = x as i32;
285            let p2 = sample_x(src, src_x - 1, y, src_width, edge_mode);
286
287            // Generate two output pixels per input with phase-aligned interpolation:
288            // output[2x]   = 0.25×p2 + 0.75×p1  (position 2x   is 0.5 from center at 2x+0.5)
289            // output[2x+1] = 0.75×p1 + 0.25×p0  (position 2x+1 is 0.5 from center at 2x+0.5)
290            let dst_x = x * 2;
291            src.set_pixel(dst_x, y, interpolate_25_75(p2, p1));
292            src.set_pixel(dst_x + 1, y, interpolate_75_25(p1, p0));
293
294            // Advance sliding window for next iteration
295            p0 = p1;
296            p1 = p2;
297        }
298    }
299}
300
301/// Vertical upsampling pass using [0.75, 0.25] interpolation with logical dimensions.
302///
303/// Doubles the logical height using phase-aligned interpolation. Each input pixel
304/// generates two output pixels with different weights based on their distance from
305/// the downsampled pixel's center position.
306/// Operates in-place by processing backwards to avoid overwriting source data.
307fn upscale_y(src: &mut Pixmap, src_width: u16, src_height: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) {
308    // Process backwards (bottom to top) to avoid overwriting source data
309    for x in 0..src_width {
310        // Maintain sliding window of three pixels: prev, current, next
311        // This allows us to compute both output pixels that depend on current pixel y
312        let mut p0 = sample_y(src, x, src_height as i32, src_height, edge_mode);
313        let mut p1 = sample_y(src, x, src_height as i32 - 1, src_height, edge_mode);
314
315        for y in (0..src_height).rev() {
316            let src_y = y as i32;
317            let p2 = sample_y(src, x, src_y - 1, src_height, edge_mode);
318
319            // Generate two output rows per input with phase-aligned interpolation:
320            // output[2y]   = 0.25×p2 + 0.75×p1  (position 2y   is 0.5 from center at 2y+0.5)
321            // output[2y+1] = 0.75×p1 + 0.25×p0  (position 2y+1 is 0.5 from center at 2y+0.5)
322            let dst_y = y * 2;
323            src.set_pixel(x, dst_y, interpolate_25_75(p2, p1));
324            src.set_pixel(x, dst_y + 1, interpolate_75_25(p1, p0));
325
326            // Advance sliding window for next iteration
327            p0 = p1;
328            p1 = p2;
329        }
330    }
331}

333/// Transparent black pixel constant.
334const TRANSPARENT_BLACK: PremulRgba8 = PremulRgba8 { r: 0, g: 0, b: 0, a: 0 };
335
336/// Sample a pixel with edge mode handling for horizontal sampling.
337#[inline(always)]
338fn sample_x(src: &Pixmap, x: i32, y: u16, width: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) -> PremulRgba8 {
339    sample(x, width, edge_mode, |src_x| src.sample(src_x, y))
340}
341
342/// Sample a pixel with edge mode handling for vertical sampling.
343#[inline(always)]
344fn sample_y(src: &Pixmap, x: u16, y: i32, height: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) -> PremulRgba8 {
345    sample(y, height, edge_mode, |src_y| src.sample(x, src_y))
346}
347
348/// Sample a pixel with edge mode handling (generic implementation).
349///
350/// Handles both horizontal and vertical sampling based on the provided closure.
351/// The `sample_fn` closure receives the clamped/extended coordinate and returns the pixel.
352/// For `EdgeMode::None`, returns transparent black if the coordinate is out of bounds.
353#[inline(always)]
354fn sample<F>(coord: i32, size: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode, sample_fn: F) -> PremulRgba8
355where
356    F: FnOnce(u16) -> PremulRgba8,
357{
358    // For EdgeMode::None, return transparent black if out of bounds
359    if edge_mode == EdgeMode::None && (coord < 0 || coord >= size as i32) {
360        return TRANSPARENT_BLACK;
361    }
362    let extended_coord = extend(coord, size, edge_mode);
363    sample_fn(extended_coord)
364}
365
366/// Extend a coordinate beyond image boundaries according to the edge mode.
367///
368/// Transforms out-of-bounds coordinates for sampling: clamped, wrapped, or mirrored
369/// depending on the mode. For `EdgeMode::None`, the coordinate is guaranteed to be
370/// in-bounds (already checked by caller, which returns transparent black for out-of-bounds).
371#[inline(always)]
372fn extend(coord: i32, size: u16, edge_mode: EdgeMode) -> u16 {
373    match edge_mode {
374        EdgeMode::Duplicate => {
375            // Clamp to image bounds: pixels outside use nearest edge pixel
376            coord.clamp(0, size as i32 - 1) as u16
377        }
378        EdgeMode::None => {
379            // Coordinate is already validated as in-bounds by caller
380            coord as u16
381        }
382        EdgeMode::Wrap => {
383            // Wrap around using modulo: image tiles infinitely
384            let mut c = coord % size as i32;
385            if c < 0 {
386                c += size as i32;
387            }
388            c as u16
389        }
390        EdgeMode::Mirror => {
391            // Mirror at boundaries: image reflects across edges
392            let period = size as i32 * 2;
393            let mut c = coord % period;
394            if c < 0 {
395                c += period;
396            }
397            if c >= size as i32 {
398                c = period - c - 1;
399            }
400            c as u16
401        }
402    }
403}

405/// Blend 4 RGBA pixels using \[1,3,3,1\]/8 binomial weights.
406///
407/// Computes `(p0 + 3×p1 + 3×p2 + p3) / 8` using efficient integer arithmetic (right shift).
408/// This binomial pattern approximates a Gaussian and contributes variance=0.75 to the blur.
409/// Adds 4 before the shift to implement round-to-nearest instead of floor division.
410#[inline(always)]
411fn decimate_weighted(p0: PremulRgba8, p1: PremulRgba8, p2: PremulRgba8, p3: PremulRgba8) -> PremulRgba8 {
412    let r = ((p0.r as u32 + p1.r as u32 * 3 + p2.r as u32 * 3 + p3.r as u32 + 4) >> 3) as u8;
413    let g = ((p0.g as u32 + p1.g as u32 * 3 + p2.g as u32 * 3 + p3.g as u32 + 4) >> 3) as u8;
414    let b = ((p0.b as u32 + p1.b as u32 * 3 + p2.b as u32 * 3 + p3.b as u32 + 4) >> 3) as u8;
415    let a = ((p0.a as u32 + p1.a as u32 * 3 + p2.a as u32 * 3 + p3.a as u32 + 4) >> 3) as u8;
416    PremulRgba8 { r, g, b, a }
417}
418
419/// Blend 2 RGBA pixels using [0.25, 0.75] weights (right-weighted interpolation).
420///
421/// Used for upsampling to generate the second of two output pixels.
422/// Favors the right/next pixel (p1) with 75% weight.
423/// Adds 2 before the shift to implement round-to-nearest instead of floor division.
424#[inline(always)]
425fn interpolate_25_75(p0: PremulRgba8, p1: PremulRgba8) -> PremulRgba8 {
426    let r = ((p0.r as u32 + p1.r as u32 * 3 + 2) >> 2) as u8;
427    let g = ((p0.g as u32 + p1.g as u32 * 3 + 2) >> 2) as u8;
428    let b = ((p0.b as u32 + p1.b as u32 * 3 + 2) >> 2) as u8;
429    let a = ((p0.a as u32 + p1.a as u32 * 3 + 2) >> 2) as u8;
430    PremulRgba8 { r, g, b, a }
431}
432
433/// Blend 2 RGBA pixels using [0.75, 0.25] weights.
434///
435/// Computes `0.75×p0 + 0.25×p1` using efficient integer arithmetic.
436/// Used during upsampling for positions closer to the first pixel.
437/// Adds 2 before the shift to implement round-to-nearest instead of floor division.
438#[inline(always)]
439fn interpolate_75_25(p0: PremulRgba8, p1: PremulRgba8) -> PremulRgba8 {
440    let r = ((p0.r as u32 * 3 + p1.r as u32 + 2) >> 2) as u8;
441    let g = ((p0.g as u32 * 3 + p1.g as u32 + 2) >> 2) as u8;
442    let b = ((p0.b as u32 * 3 + p1.b as u32 + 2) >> 2) as u8;
443    let a = ((p0.a as u32 * 3 + p1.a as u32 + 2) >> 2) as u8;
444    PremulRgba8 { r, g, b, a }
445}

447#[cfg(any())]
448mod tests {
449    use super::*;
450    use crate::third_party::vello_common::filter::gaussian_blur::{MAX_KERNEL_SIZE, compute_gaussian_kernel, plan_decimated_blur};
451
452    /// Test edge extension with Duplicate mode.
453    #[cfg(any())]
454    fn test_extend_duplicate() {
455        let size = 10;
456
457        // In-bounds coordinate
458        assert_eq!(extend(5, size, EdgeMode::Duplicate), 5);
459
460        // Below bounds: clamp to 0
461        assert_eq!(extend(-1, size, EdgeMode::Duplicate), 0);
462        assert_eq!(extend(-10, size, EdgeMode::Duplicate), 0);
463
464        // Above bounds: clamp to size-1
465        assert_eq!(extend(10, size, EdgeMode::Duplicate), 9);
466        assert_eq!(extend(20, size, EdgeMode::Duplicate), 9);
467    }
468
469    /// Test edge extension with Wrap mode.
470    #[cfg(any())]
471    fn test_extend_wrap() {
472        let size = 10;
473
474        // In-bounds: identity
475        assert_eq!(extend(5, size, EdgeMode::Wrap), 5);
476
477        // Above bounds: wrap around
478        assert_eq!(extend(10, size, EdgeMode::Wrap), 0);
479        assert_eq!(extend(11, size, EdgeMode::Wrap), 1);
480        assert_eq!(extend(25, size, EdgeMode::Wrap), 5);
481
482        // Below bounds: wrap from end
483        assert_eq!(extend(-1, size, EdgeMode::Wrap), 9);
484        assert_eq!(extend(-2, size, EdgeMode::Wrap), 8);
485    }
486
487    /// Test edge extension with Mirror mode.
488    #[cfg(any())]
489    fn test_extend_mirror() {
490        let size = 10;
491
492        // In-bounds: identity
493        assert_eq!(extend(5, size, EdgeMode::Mirror), 5);
494
495        // Just past boundary: mirror back
496        // For coord=10: period=20, c=10, c>=10 so c = 20-10-1 = 9
497        assert_eq!(extend(10, size, EdgeMode::Mirror), 9);
498        // For coord=11: period=20, c=11, c>=10 so c = 20-11-1 = 8
499        assert_eq!(extend(11, size, EdgeMode::Mirror), 8);
500
501        // Full reflection cycle (period = 2*size = 20)
502        // For coord=19: c=19, c>=10 so c = 20-19-1 = 0
503        assert_eq!(extend(19, size, EdgeMode::Mirror), 0);
504        // For coord=20: c=20%20=0, c<10 so c=0
505        assert_eq!(extend(20, size, EdgeMode::Mirror), 0);
506
507        // Negative coordinates
508        // For coord=-1: c=-1%20=-1, c<0 so c+=20 → c=19, c>=10 so c=20-19-1=0
509        assert_eq!(extend(-1, size, EdgeMode::Mirror), 0);
510        // For coord=-2: c=-2%20=-2, c<0 so c+=20 → c=18, c>=10 so c=20-18-1=1
511        assert_eq!(extend(-2, size, EdgeMode::Mirror), 1);
512    }

521        assert_eq!(extend(10, size, EdgeMode::None), 10);

525    /// Test [1,3,3,1]/8 decimation weights.
526    #[cfg(any())]
527    fn test_decimate_weighted() {
528        let p0 = PremulRgba8 { r: 0, g: 0, b: 0, a: 0 };
529        let p1 = PremulRgba8 { r: 8, g: 8, b: 8, a: 8 };
530        let p2 = PremulRgba8 { r: 8, g: 8, b: 8, a: 8 };
531        let p3 = PremulRgba8 { r: 0, g: 0, b: 0, a: 0 };
532
533        // (0 + 3*8 + 3*8 + 0 + 4) / 8 = (48 + 4) / 8 = 52 / 8 = 6.5 → 6 (rounds down)
534        let result = decimate_weighted(p0, p1, p2, p3);
535        assert_eq!(result.r, 6);
536        assert_eq!(result.g, 6);
537        assert_eq!(result.b, 6);
538        assert_eq!(result.a, 6);
539    }

545        let result = decimate_weighted(p, p, p, p);
546        // All same: (100 + 300 + 300 + 100 + 4) / 8 = 804/8 = 100.5 → 100 (rounds down)
547        assert_eq!(result.r, 100);
548        assert_eq!(result.g, 150);
549        assert_eq!(result.b, 200);
550        assert_eq!(result.a, 255);

581    /// Test interpolation symmetry.

646
647        let (kernel, kernel_size) = compute_gaussian_kernel(1.0);
648        convolve_x(&src, &mut dst, 5, 3, &kernel[..usize::from(kernel_size)], kernel_size / 2, EdgeMode::Duplicate);

652            for x in 0..5 {
653                let pixel = dst.sample(x, y);
654                assert_eq!(pixel, PremulRgba8 { r: 128, g: 128, b: 128, a: 255 });

693    /// Test that large sigma values are clamped to `MAX_KERNEL_SIZE`.
694    #[cfg(any())]
695    fn test_large_sigma_clamped_to_max() {
696        let (kernel, kernel_size) = compute_gaussian_kernel(100.0);
697        // For σ=100, radius = ceil(300) = 300, size would be 601
698        // But it should be clamped to MAX_KERNEL_SIZE
699        assert_eq!(usize::from(kernel_size), MAX_KERNEL_SIZE);
700
701        // The clamped kernel should still sum to 1.0 (normalized)
702        let sum: f32 = kernel.iter().take(usize::from(kernel_size)).sum();
703        assert!((sum - 1.0).abs() < 1e-6);
704    }

714    /// Test sampling behavior at exact boundaries for each edge mode.
715    #[cfg(any())]
716    fn test_sample_x_at_boundaries() {
717        let mut pixmap = Pixmap::new(3, 1);
718        pixmap.set_pixel(0, 0, PremulRgba8 { r: 10, g: 0, b: 0, a: 255 });
719        pixmap.set_pixel(1, 0, PremulRgba8 { r: 20, g: 0, b: 0, a: 255 });
720        pixmap.set_pixel(2, 0, PremulRgba8 { r: 30, g: 0, b: 0, a: 255 });
721
722        // Test left boundary with Duplicate
723        let mut p = sample_x(&pixmap, -1, 0, 3, EdgeMode::Duplicate);
724        assert_eq!(p.r, 10); // Should clamp to first pixel
725
726        // Test right boundary with Duplicate
727        p = sample_x(&pixmap, 3, 0, 3, EdgeMode::Duplicate);
728        assert_eq!(p.r, 30); // Should clamp to last pixel
729
730        // Test with None mode (should return transparent black)
731        p = sample_x(&pixmap, -1, 0, 3, EdgeMode::None);
732        assert_eq!(p.a, 0);
733    }

782    fn pixmap_from_red(width: u16, height: u16, values: &[&[u8]]) -> Pixmap {
783        let mut pixmap = Pixmap::new(width, height);
784        for (y, row) in values.iter().enumerate() {
785            for (x, &r) in row.iter().enumerate() {
786                pixmap.set_pixel(x as u16, y as u16, PremulRgba8 { r, g: 0, b: 0, a: 255 });
787            }
788        }
789        pixmap
790    }
791
792    fn assert_red_values<const W: usize, const H: usize>(pixmap: &Pixmap, expected: [[u8; W]; H]) {
793        for (y, row) in expected.iter().enumerate() {
794            for (x, &want) in row.iter().enumerate() {
795                let got = pixmap.sample(x as u16, y as u16).r;
796
797                assert_eq!(got, want, "red mismatch at ({x}, {y}): got {got}, expected {want}");
798            }
799        }
800    }

802    #[cfg(any())]
803    fn test_downscale_x_non_uniform() {
804        //   (0,0)=0    (1,0)=40   (2,0)=80   (3,0)=120
805        //   (0,1)=20   (1,1)=60   (2,1)=100  (3,1)=140
806        let mut pixmap = pixmap_from_red(4, 2, &[&[0, 40, 80, 120], &[20, 60, 100, 140]]);
807
808        let dst_width = 4_u16.div_ceil(2);
809        downscale_x(&mut pixmap, 4, 2, dst_width, EdgeMode::Duplicate);
810
811        // Row 0: p[-1]=0,p[0]=0,p[1]=40,p[2]=80    → (0+0*3+40*3+80+4)>>3       = 25
812        //        p[1]=40,p[2]=80,p[3]=120,p[4]=120  → (40+80*3+120*3+120+4)>>3   = 95
813        // Row 1: p[-1]=20,p[0]=20,p[1]=60,p[2]=100  → (20+20*3+60*3+100+4)>>3    = 45
814        //        p[1]=60,p[2]=100,p[3]=140,p[4]=140  → (60+100*3+140*3+140+4)>>3   = 115
815        assert_red_values(&pixmap, [[25, 95], [45, 115]]);
816    }

818    #[cfg(any())]
819    fn test_downscale_y_non_uniform() {
820        // Use a 2x4 image (output of a prior downscale_x).
821        //   (0,0)=25   (1,0)=95
822        //   (0,1)=45   (1,1)=115
823        //   (0,2)=35   (1,2)=105
824        //   (0,3)=55   (1,3)=125
825        let mut pixmap = pixmap_from_red(2, 4, &[&[25, 95], &[45, 115], &[35, 105], &[55, 125]]);
826
827        let dst_height = 4_u16.div_ceil(2);
828        downscale_y(&mut pixmap, 2, 4, dst_height, EdgeMode::Duplicate);
829
830        // Col 0: p[-1]=25,p[0]=25,p[1]=45,p[2]=35 → (25+25*3+45*3+35+4)>>3   = 34
831        //        p[1]=45,p[2]=35,p[3]=55,p[4]=55   → (45+35*3+55*3+55+4)>>3  = 46
832        // Col 1: p[-1]=95,p[0]=95,p[1]=115,p[2]=105 → (95+95*3+115*3+105+4)>>3 = 104
833        //        p[1]=115,p[2]=105,p[3]=125,p[4]=125 → (115+105*3+125*3+125+4)>>3 = 116
834        assert_red_values(&pixmap, [[34, 104], [46, 116]]);
835    }
